operating_model_json.business_description_summary: Halbrook Grounds Management is a commercial grounds maintenance and landscaping company serving office parks, HOAs, and property managers on the Kansas side of the KC metro. Work is fulfilled by in-house crews running scheduled maintenance routes and dedicated install crews, loading trucks and equipment at the yard each morning and working on-site at client properties. The primary unit of work is a Maintenance contract-month and Install job delivered on a monthly and contract cadence for maintenance contracts, and one contract-sized install job from start to finish for installation work. Typical lead times for new work are days to a few weeks, with maintenance visits occurring on fixed route days and install projects booked into open calendar windows; overall capacity is constrained mainly by labor (crew hours and daylight) rather than demand or software systems. Standard licensing, insurance, and safety/compliance practices for commercial grounds maintenance and landscape installation in Kansas are assumed to be in place (e.g., business registration as a S-corp, appropriate liability/auto coverage, and any applicable equipment, environmental, and site-safety requirements), with exact requirements depending on local jurisdiction and specific service scope.

people.role_title: Owner; sales lead and field operations
people.primary_responsibilities: Leads sales and bidding with property managers, oversees field operations for both maintenance routes and install projects, manages client relationships, and ensures quality, safety, and schedule adherence across all routes and jobs.
people.relevant_background: Nineteen years in commercial landscaping, including six years running Halbrook Grounds Management, supported by a two-year turf management degree and a Kansas pesticide applicator license.
people.why_strengthens_business: Rafael’s deep technical knowledge, licensing, and long-standing industry experience allow him to price and scope work accurately, maintain quality across multiple crews, and build the long-term client relationships that underpin recurring maintenance contracts and profitable install work.
people.paragraph: Rafael Ostrowski serves as Owner and leads both sales and field operations for Halbrook Grounds Management, bringing nineteen years of commercial landscaping experience, including six years running the company. With a two-year turf management degree and a Kansas pesticide applicator license, he combines technical expertise with practical route and crew management. Rafael personally handles bids and site walks with property managers and oversees day-to-day execution on both maintenance routes and install projects, which ensures accurate pricing, consistent quality, and reliable delivery across the portfolio of commercial properties.

people.primary_responsibilities: Leads the maintenance crews on scheduled routes, organizes daily work at the yard and on-site, manages mowing, trimming, and clean-up standards, and addresses minor equipment issues to keep the route on schedule.
people.relevant_background: Five years of experience in the business, all with Halbrook Grounds Management, with hands-on expertise running commercial maintenance routes and troubleshooting equipment in the field.
people.why_strengthens_business: Ignacio’s reliability, route leadership, and mechanical know-how allow Halbrook Grounds Management to keep a full book of recurring properties on schedule with consistent quality, directly supporting the stability and renewal of its maintenance contracts.
people.paragraph: Ignacio Ferreira-Sandoval is the crew lead responsible for running the maintenance routes at Halbrook Grounds Management, bringing five years of in-house experience on the company’s commercial properties. He organizes daily work for the maintenance crews, ensures mowing, trimming, and clean-up are completed to standard on each visit, and uses his ability to fix equipment issues in the field to minimize downtime. Ignacio’s steady leadership on route keeps recurring properties serviced reliably and protects the continuity and reputation of the maintenance contract side of the business.

people.role_title: Crew lead; runs install crew and does takeoffs
people.primary_responsibilities: Leads the install crew on-site, coordinates installation sequencing and site logistics, performs takeoffs and basic scoping for new beds, irrigation, and sod jobs, and works with ownership to ensure jobs are executed to spec and budget.
people.relevant_background: Four years of experience with Halbrook Grounds Management running commercial install work, supported by a horticulture certificate that underpins plant selection, layout, and installation practices.
people.why_strengthens_business: Bethany’s combination of hands-on install leadership and horticultural training enables Halbrook Grounds Management to deliver higher-margin projects efficiently and professionally, turning bids into well-executed jobs that complement the recurring maintenance book.
people.paragraph: Bethany Kowalczyk leads the install crew for Halbrook Grounds Management and handles takeoffs for new beds, irrigation, and sod projects, drawing on four years of experience with the company and a horticulture certificate. She coordinates on-site installation work, manages crew activities and sequencing, and supports accurate scoping so that install jobs are bid and delivered in line with expectations. Bethany’s role converts install opportunities into well-executed, higher-margin projects that fit smoothly alongside the maintenance routes and strengthen the company’s value to commercial property managers.

marketing_model_json.marketing_basis_summary:
Business stage: operating, with six years of history and owner-led relationship sales, but the plan is framed like a focused ramp year targeting a clear commercial segment in one county.

B2B reach: The CBP universe shows 1,697 establishments in the relevant NAICS bands in Kansas, including Johnson County. Halbrook’s true buyers are a narrower role-based group: established commercial property owners and management firms (office parks, medical campuses, HOAs, non‑retail commercial) that control multiple buildings and value stable crews. Within the Johnson County footprint (Overland Park, Lenexa, Shawnee, Olathe, Leawood), only a subset of those 1,697 are relevant and realistically reachable in Year 1 via Rafael’s bandwidth, in‑person networking, LinkedIn outreach, and referrals. Treating the Johnson County slice plus the relevant size/age filters as roughly one-third of the state-level establishments, and then further limiting to non‑retail multi‑property managers and suitable HOAs, yields an order‑of‑magnitude reachable universe of about 200–250 firms for planning. We anchor reachable_market_b2b at 220 firms as a realistic Year‑1 reachable subset of the CBP universe, not the full set of establishments.

Demand vs. reach: Year‑1 revenue of $1.4M comes from ~398 maintenance contract‑months plus ~25 install jobs (≈422 total units). At an average of ~1.9 units per reachable firm, that can be supported by ~22 active client relationships if each controls multiple properties and/or books periodic install projects. A capture_rate_year1 of 1.92 units per reachable firm does not mean nearly 200% adoption; it reflects the unit structure: a single property on contract generates 12 maintenance contract‑months per year, and many target clients manage several properties plus occasional install work. Converting roughly 10% of reachable firms (≈22 of 220) into active customers at this multi‑unit usage level fits the relationship-based, route-driven model.

Marketing baseline: Channels are primarily targeted and relationship-based (LinkedIn outreach to known roles, BOMA/IFMA style groups, chamber/property associations, referrals, some search presence). These tend to be lower cash‑spend but higher time‑intensity, with modest paid media (Google/search, directory listings) and heavier investment in networking, association dues, and sales time. For an operating, owner‑led commercial grounds firm with strong word-of-mouth potential and local focus, a baseline marketing spend of about 8% of Year‑1 revenue is appropriate: enough budget to support memberships, modest digital, and consistent prospecting without assuming heavy paid lead-gen or brand advertising. This supports acquiring ~20–25 route‑fit accounts while staying realistic about owner bandwidth and relationship-driven sales.

Combined reachable_market: The 220 figure is a planning/reporting view of the reachable B2B firm universe in Johnson County for Year 1. There is no B2C component for this model, so reachable_market_b2c is 0. The combined reachable_market should not be read as a literal homogeneous TAM, but as the number of distinct firms that the described channels and sales model can plausibly touch and qualify in the first year.
